rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces are one shared word used for several senses; counterparts are words with a single shared sense, as the listed senses of huda illustrate.
rows.anchor: فالوجوه اللفظ المشترك الذى يستعمل فى عدة معان كلفظ الأمة والنظائر كالألفاظ المتواطئة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The alternative that faces concern meanings while counterparts concern wording is weak, since the books classify a single word's varied uses as faces.
rows.anchor: وقيل النظائر فى اللفظ والوجوه فى المعانى وضعف لأنه لو أريد هذا لكان الجمع فى الألفاظ المشتركة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some classify the many senses a single Qur'anic word can bear as a form of inimitability unavailable in human speech.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل بعضهم ذلك من أنواع معجزات القرآن حيث كانت الكلمة الواحدة تنصرف إلى عشرين وجها أو أكثر أو أقل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muqatil cites a marfuʿ report that full understanding of Qur'an requires recognizing its many possible senses; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: وذكر مقاتل فى صدر كتابه حديثا مرفوعا لا يكون الرجل فقيها كل الفقه حتى يرى للقرآن وجوها كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean clarification or explanation.
rows.anchor: أولئك على هدى من ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean the religion of God.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الدين ﴿ إن الهدى هدى الله ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean faith.
rows.anchor: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related forms can mean a guide or caller, as in the guide for every people and leaders guiding by God's command.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الداعى ﴿ ولكل قوم هاد ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can refer collectively to messengers and revealed books.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الرسل والكتب ﴿ فإما يأتينكم مني هدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the statement about finding one's way by the stars, huda means knowledge.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى المعرفة ﴿ وبالنجم هم يهتدون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Fatiha petition, huda means right guidance or rectitude.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الرشاد ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-huda in the cited passages can refer to Muhammad, peace be upon him.
rows.anchor: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-huda that came to them from their Lord means the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the statement about what Moses received, huda means the Torah.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى التوراة ﴿ ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can denote istirjaʿ: recognizing in calamity that it comes from God and saying the prescribed return formula.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الاسترجاع ﴿ وأولئك هم المهتدون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here God's not guiding wrongdoers means not guiding them to the proof in Abraham's argument.
rows.anchor: والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A good stop gives a complete sense, though what follows remains attached in wording or meaning and cannot be begun independently; the Fatiha examples illustrate it.
rows.anchor: والحسن هو الذى يحسن الوقوف عليه ولا يحسن الابتداء بما بعده لتعلقه به فى اللفظ والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bad stop obscures the intended sense, including breaks between an adjective and its noun, a substitute and its antecedent, or a preposition and its object.
rows.anchor: القبيح هو الذى لا يفهم منه المراد نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping so that the next words falsely identify Jesus or another as God is especially heinous; deliberately intending that meaning is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وأقبح من هذا الوقف على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping at a negation before its affirmative exception is even worse; if breath forces a pause, resume before the break and connect the rest.
rows.anchor: وأقبح من هذا وأشنع الوقف على النفى دون حروف الإيجاب نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One classification calls a stop sufficient when the next verse has verbal attachment, good and sufficient when attachment is semantic, complete when neither holds, and bad when the sense conflicts; 1:6 continues verbally into 1:7.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن تعلقت الآية بما قبلها تعلقا لفظيا كان الوقف كافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated declaration that none is god but God closes with what it began, fitting the description of God as First and Last.
rows.anchor: وقوله لا إله إلا الله كررها وختم بها في قوله

words: من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says one prayer upon him is answered by ten prayers from God, corresponding to the tenfold reward for a good deed.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلوا علي فإنه من صلى على واحدة صلى الله عليه بها عشرا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs his followers to ask God for the wasila, linked here with the promised praiseworthy station and the command to seek nearness to God.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم سلوا الله لي الوسيلة فى قوله

words: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever intercedes for him will have his intercession on the Day of Resurrection, associated with the verse promising a share to the good intercessor.
rows.anchor: وقوله حلت له شفاعتى يوم القيامة فى قوله ﴿ من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ﴾

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Muslim's prayer for an absent fellow Muslim is answered, with an attending angel saying amen and the same blessing for the supplicant; the Fatiha's plural petition also includes the community.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعوة المسلم لأخيه بظهر الغيب مستجابة عند رأسه ملك وكل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first al-balad means Mecca and the second may mean Medina, alluding to both sacred cities; repeating the noun for two places and addressing both is preferable because both are inviolable.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن إبراهيم حرم مكة وأنا حرمت المدينة

rows.speaker: هذا الإمام
rows.claim: The imam says the Qur'an alludes to the Dajjal through the Samaritan's appointed promise and Israel's two corruptions, return, and final promise, which signals Jesus's emergence.
rows.anchor: ثم رأيت هذا الإمام قال إن فى القرآن تعريضا بقصته فى قصة السامري وقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed people are clarified by 4:69 as prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous; this broader verse is the best explanation of the Fatiha phrase.
rows.anchor: بينة فى آية النساء بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam's passage cannot be restricted to prophets: it includes those carried with Noah and those guided and chosen, and Maryam is a truthful woman according to one view; even if prophetic, they are only a subset.
rows.anchor: قيل لا نسلم اولا أن هذه الآية فى النبيين فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanting steadfastness on the straight path is itself obedience to God and His Messenger, since guidance to that path entails the obedience that places one with the blessed.
rows.anchor: والرغبة إلى الله تعالى فى الثبات عليها هي نفس الطاعة لله ولرسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase may be assigned to a more fitting referent than its apparent one; examples include naming the Fatiha the seven oft-repeated verses though all Qur'an is described as repeated.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون اللفظ مقتضيا لأمر ويحمل على غيره لأنه أولى بذلك الاسم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse's context includes the Prophet's wives and they cannot be excluded, the masculine address extends purification to all the Household; Ali and Fatima are especially entitled to this description.
rows.anchor: وسياق القرآن يدل على إرادة الأزواج وفيهن نزلت ولا يمكن خروجهن عن الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains that a substitute can clarify its antecedent because its governing element is understood from the antecedent and connects the two in wording.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأبي علي كيف يكون البدل إيضاحا للمبدل منه وهو من غير جملته فقال لما لم يظهر العامل في البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A substitute can make praise more forceful by stating a general description first and then naming its specific instance.
rows.anchor: ومن فوائد البدل التبيين على وجه المدح فقولك هل أدلك على أكرم الناس وأفضلهم فلان أبلغ

rows.speaker: الأخفش والواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Wahidi call the part-for-whole substitute in the pilgrimage verse a clarifying substitute: the general obligation is followed by its intended subset.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش والواحدي في بدل البعض من الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Part and inclusion substitutes clarify and specify an antecedent by naming it twice, first generally and then particularly; the forelock example adds its quality as the reason for seizing it.
rows.anchor: وفائدة البدل أن ذلك الشيء يصير مذكورا مرتين إحداهما بالعموم والثانية بالخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite noun may be replaced by another definite noun, as in the Fatiha's repeated mention of the straight path.
rows.anchor: ويجوز بدل المعرفة من المعرفة نحو ﴿ الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن يعيش
rows.claim: Ibn Yaʿish says an indefinite substitute for a definite is not good unless qualified, as in the described forelock, because the clarification depends on both.
rows.anchor: قال ابن يعيش ولا يحسن بدل النكرة من المعرفة حتى توصف كالآية لأن البيان مرتبط بهما جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite may also replace another indefinite: the gardens and following items specify the felicity promised to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: حدائق وأعنابا وكواعب أترابا وكأسا دهاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase black intensely black mountains, sud is a substitute for gharabib; the original order was sud gharabib, with gharabib first serving as an adjective.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ وغرابيب سود ﴾ فان سود بدل من غرابيب لأن الأصل سود غرابيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qualified indefinite can replace another qualified indefinite, clarifying the first phrase with a description such as religion or counted dirhams.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ ومن يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا ﴾ وقوله ﴿ وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the same definite noun is repeated, the second usually refers to the first; examples include hardship in 94:5–6, the path in the Fatiha, and celestial objects in 41:37.
rows.anchor: فالأول إن يكونا معرفتين والثاني فيه هو الأول غالبا

rows.speaker: التنوخي
rows.claim: Al-Tanukhi explains that the hardship is one because the definite article denotes the unique generic kind, which is neither individually one nor numerically many.
rows.anchor: قال التنوخي إنما كان مع العسر واحدا لأن اللام طبيعة لا ثاني لها بمعنى إن الجنس هى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated definite form does not always keep one referent: good action differs from its reward, and the killer differs from the slain or free person in the retaliation examples.
rows.anchor: وهذه القاعدة ليست مطردة وهي منقوضة بآيات كثيرة كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further counterexamples repeat the same definite word for different referents, including the scripture revealed to Muhammad and earlier scripture, and God's sovereignty versus what He grants a servant.
rows.anchor: فالملك الذي يؤتيه الله للعبد لايمكن إن يكون نفس ملكه فقد اختلفا وهما معرفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun for the all-encompassing favor can refer back by the shared basic meaning of favor, even when the repeated expression does not have the same concrete referent.
rows.anchor: فقد اعاد الضمير في المنفصل المستغرق باعتبار اصل الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic verse endings use either identical letters or letters close in sound; examples include the matched moon and two nearly matched Fatiha endings.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر ﴾ وجميع هذه السورة على الازدواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because sajʿ strictly requires matching letters, the close-but-not-identical endings in these examples do not count as sajʿ even for those who apply that term to Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يسمى سجعا قطعا عند القائلين بإطلاق السجع فى القرآن لأن السجع ما تماثلت حروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts the basmala and makes the rest of 1:7 one verse; Abu Hanifa omits the basmala and divides its two phrases. Both count seven verses, but al-Shafiʿi's division better preserves the endings because anʿamta ʿalayhim does not match prior endings.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يترجح مذهب الشافعى على مذهب أبى حنيفة فى عد الفاتحة سبع آيات مع البسملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The science of ambiguous identities has dedicated books by al-Suhayli and his student Ibn ʿAsakir, and was also studied among the early generations.
rows.anchor: وقد صنف فيه أبو القاسم السهيلى كتابه المسمى بالتعريف والإعلام وتلاه تلميذه ابن عساكر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says he spent fourteen years seeking the identity of the emigrant who left home for God and His Messenger but died en route.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة طلبت الذى خرج فى بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم أدركه الموت أربع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not investigate identities that God says He alone knows; al-Zarkashi condemns claims that these unknown people were Qurayza or jinn.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه لا يبحث فيما أخبر الله باستئثاره بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people blessed in the Fatiha are identified elsewhere as prophets, truthful people, martyrs, and righteous people.
rows.anchor: من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context identifies the unnamed vicegerent in God's announcement to the angels as Adam.
rows.anchor: خليفة ﴾ والمراد آدم والسياق بينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be with the truthful is linked to the Muhajirun described in 59:8; Abu Bakr invoked it at the Saqifa, arguing that the Ansar should follow them and that he, the greatest truthful one, especially qualified.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم المهاجرون لقوله فى الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam and Jesus are called one sign in the singular because their story is one event: her bearing him without a man.
rows.anchor: وهما آيتان لأنها قضية واحدة وهى ولادتها له من غير ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identities are left unnamed because fame makes the referent unmistakable: the spouse addressed with Adam is Eve.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل حواء لأنه ليس غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unnamed disputant who argued with Abraham is Nimrod, identified as the king to whom the message was sent.
rows.anchor: والمراد النمروذ لأنه المرسل أليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unnamed purchaser of Joseph in Egypt is the Aziz.
rows.anchor: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر ﴾ والمراد العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sons of Adam in the narrative are Cain and Abel.
rows.anchor: بالحق ﴾ والمراد قابيل وهابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura endings, like openings, conclude with apt meanings and signal that the discourse has ended, releasing the listener's anticipation of what comes next.
rows.anchor: وهى مثل الفواتح فى الحسن لأنها آخر ما يقرع الأسماع فلهذا جاءت متضمنة للمعانى البديعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha closing spells out the highest request: faith and its blessings, preserved from sins that bring God's anger and from deviation beyond His limits.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أطلق الإنعام ولم يقيده ليتناول كل إنعام لأن من أنعم عليه بنعمة الإيمان فقد أنعم عليه بكل نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing of al-Baqara is another example of a sura ending made of supplication.
rows.anchor: وكالدعاء الذى اشتملت عليه الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali Imran ends with commands to patience in religious duties, perseverance against enemies and in war, frontier vigilance, and God-consciousness; taqwa promises an opening and provision, and God's laʿalla is certain.
rows.anchor: وكالوصايا التى ختمت بها سورة آل عمران بالصبر على تكاليف الدين والمصابرة لأعداء الله فى الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending of al-Nisa is apt because it contains the final legal rulings revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وكالوصايا والفرائض التى ختمت بها سورة النساء وحسن الختم بها لأنها آخر ما نزل من الأحكام عام حجة الوداع

words: لله ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيهن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Maida's closing glorifies God; the relative pronoun ma rather than man is chosen for emphatic generality across every kind of thing.
rows.anchor: ولإرادة المبالغة فى التعظيم أختيرت ما على من لإفادة العموم فيتناول الأجناس كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive praises intensify the servant's attention: God's exclusive praise, universal lordship, gifts of mercy, and command of judgment prepare the worshipper to approach and seek help.
rows.anchor: فإن العبد إذا افتتح حمد مولاه بقوله الحمد لله الدال على اختصاصه بالحمد وجد من نفسه التحرك للإقبال عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says praise uses third person because it ranks below worship, while direct address elevates the worshipper's encounter; similarly, blessing is explicitly attributed to God but anger is phrased obliquely as a matter of etiquette.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنما اختير للحمد لفظ الغيبة وللعبادة الخطاب للإشارة إلى أن الحمد دون العبادة في الرتبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says that after describing God with magnificent attributes, the discourse directly addresses the clearly identified one worthy of exclusive worship and reliance.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد وأجرى عليه بالصفات العظيمة من كونه ربا للعالمين ورحمانا ورحيما

words: وإن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A declarative sentence can stand in for a purpose clause: the statement that God is their Lord conveys therefore they should fear Him.
rows.anchor: أي ولأني ربكم فاتقون فوضع الجملة من المبتدأ والخبر موضع المفعول له

words: أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This analysis undercuts an argument based on the proclamation in 9:3: its wording can be parsed as a proclamation that both God and His Messenger are free of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يبطل تعلق من تعلق على ثبوته في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural forms can serve for either few or many because they share the general sense of plurality; one explanation says the generic article makes al-ghurufat comprehensive while signaling that only few believers dwell there.
rows.anchor: لأن الجموع يقع بعضها موقع بعض لاشتراكها في مطلق الجمعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported explanation links the generic plural in the elevated chambers to the small number of their inhabitants, since only believers enter them.
rows.anchor: وقيل سبب ذلك في الآية الأولى دخول الألف واللام الجنسية فيكون ذلك تكثيرا لها

words: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي
rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads Abraham's followers here as those who followed him during the interregnum, an example of precedence by time.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية المراد بالذين اتبعوه في زمن الفترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Sunni doctrine ranks humans above angels, angels are mentioned first because they existed earlier.
rows.anchor: فإن مذهب أهل السنة تفضيل البشر وإنما قدم الملك لسبقه في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wives precede daughters because they came earlier in time, although the daughters are superior as parts of the Prophet himself.
rows.anchor: فإن الأزواج أسبق بالزمان لأن البنات أفضل منهن لكونهن بضعة منه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of spouses before descendants is another example of precedence by time.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Precedence by time can combine with honor, as in these ordered lists of chosen figures and scriptures.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه ينضم إليه مع ذلك التشريف كقوله ﴿ إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses precedes Abraham in 53:36 because the argument concerns abandonment and Moses's scriptures were more widely circulated; the order also accommodates the verse endings.
rows.anchor: فإنما قدم ذكر موسى لوجهين أحدهما أنه في سياق الاحتجاج عليهم بالترك وكانت صحف موسى منتشرة أكثر انتشارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting those under wrath before those astray may convey disparagement: Jews preceded Christians historically and were nearer to the Muslims.
rows.anchor: تقدم اليهود لأنهم كانوا أسبق من النصارى ولأنهم كانوا أقرب إلى المؤمنين بالمجاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some sequences, such as mentioning Ad before Thamud, need not reflect the preceding temporal or honor-based rationale.
rows.anchor: وقد لا يلحظ هذا كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: The order of drowsiness before sleep follows ordinary human experience, in which drowsiness comes first.
rows.anchor: لأن العادة في البشر أن تأخذ العبد السنة قبل النوم فجاءت العبارة على حسب هذه العادة ذكره السهيلي

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli also explains that, in praise, denying even drowsiness is a stronger declaration of transcendence, since sleep is even more impossible for God.
rows.anchor: ذكره السهيلي وذكر معه وجها آخر وهو أنها وردت فى معرض التمدح والثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness precedes light in perception, and ignorance precedes spiritual understanding; being born without knowledge illustrates this precedence.
rows.anchor: فإن الظلمات سابقة على النور في الإحساس وكذلك الظلمة المعنوية سابقة على النور المعنوي
